sources.title: Gerald Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (17 November 2017)
sources.locator: §5.1, printed pp137–140: gauge introduction, Lemma 5.1, Theorems 5.2–5.3 and Corollary 5.4 through its proof (PDF indices149–152); §5.4 introduction and Lemma 5.15 through proof, printed pp149–151 (indices161–163). Not a claim to have read the rest of §5.4.

contents.name: §5.1 topological vector space and continuous dual conventions
contents.support: Joint continuity; real and complex fields.

contents.name: §5.1 Minkowski functional (5.1)
contents.support: Infimum over positive dilates; add explicit general absorption and infimum prerequisites.

contents.name: Lemma 5.1
contents.support: Convexity proof of subadditivity and strict open sublevel. Local proof supplies continuity via U∩(-U).

contents.name: Theorems 5.2 and 5.3
contents.support: Real dominated extension and complex real-part conversion; correct the displayed one-sided domination and difference-set signs as explained in notes.

contents.name: Corollary 5.4
contents.support: Finite thickening cover and maximum of the separating functional on the compact set; local cover uses all admissible witnesses.

contents.name: §5.1 gauge examples: norm ball and cylindrical strip
contents.support: Zero directions show seminorms need not be norms.

contents.name: §5.1 gauge example: nonabsorbing strip (-1,1)×{0}
contents.reason: This example has infinite gauge values outside its span, whereas the assigned gauge definition is for open absorbing zero-neighborhoods.

contents.name: §5.1 c0 lexicographic cone without an open-side separation hypothesis
contents.reason: This is a normed-space warning; the assigned B scope consists of the product examples and convex-maximum face counterexample.

contents.name: §5.4 definition and finite-seminorm neighborhood sets (5.13)
contents.support: Compare seminorm convention with convex zero-neighborhoods; general topology-generation equivalence is not assumed.

contents.name: §5.4 joint-continuity computations and Hausdorff separated-seminorm test
contents.support: Apply the finite-coordinate computations to scalar coordinate seminorms, with zero-valued coordinates handled directly.

contents.name: §5.4 examples: norm, weak and weak-star topologies
contents.reason: Specific weak-topology comparisons belong to the later weak and weak-star page; only the TVS conventions are needed here.

contents.name: §5.4 examples: strong/weak operator topologies and pointwise C(I)
contents.reason: Operator and function-space topology examples are separate from the assigned scalar product examples.

contents.name: Lemma 5.15: finite-seminorm continuity domination criterion
contents.reason: The assigned separation argument proves its needed functional continuity directly from a gauge bound; the full general criterion belongs with weak-topology finite-coordinate factorization.

contents.name: §5.4 translation invariance and linear continuity at zero
contents.support: Translations and nonzero dilations are justified from joint continuity in the local calculus supplier.

sources.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar Salamon, Functional Analysis (8 June 2017)
sources.locator: Definition 3.1 (p118), Example 3.7 (p121), Lemma 3.10 and Theorem 3.11 with complete proofs (pp123–124); additionally Definition 2.37 and complete Theorem 2.38 proof (pp76–77), and Corollary 2.36 proof (p75). Other material in §§3.1.1–3.1.2 was consulted selectively, not harvested as a completely read continuous range.

contents.name: Definition 3.1
contents.support: No Hausdorffness built into the definition.

contents.name: Definition 3.1, local convexity clause
contents.support: Open convex neighborhood convention.

contents.name: Example 3.7
contents.support: Product scalar topology; extend the real example explicitly to complex coordinates.

contents.name: Example 3.7, continuous coordinate projections
contents.support: The separator and its positive gap are calculated locally.

contents.name: Lemma 3.10, closure and interior convexity
contents.support: Neighborhood proof read in full; supplies the closure part before refinement.

contents.name: Lemma 3.10, closure of interior for convex sets with nonempty interior
contents.support: The radial interior approximation is included in the scaffold strategy.

contents.name: Theorem 3.11
contents.support: Independent real separation comparison; orientation reversed by negation, not a direct use of ordered-cone extension.

contents.name: Corollary 2.36: complexification of a real functional
contents.support: Verify H(x)-iH(ix) and real-part convention explicitly; no norm bound imported.

contents.name: Definition 2.37 and Theorem 2.38: positive extension on a cofinal ordered subspace
contents.reason: Read the complete infimum-envelope argument to understand the independent separation treatment. The assigned proof uses direct real gauge domination, so an ordered-vector-space theory is not a local prerequisite.

contents.name: Theorem 3.12 and Lemmas 3.13–3.14: finite-functional topology and kernel factorization
contents.reason: These statements and parts of the proofs were consulted while locating separation; full harvesting belongs to the later weak-topology page and is not certified here.

sources.title: Harald Hanche-Olsen, Topological vector spaces, version 1.6
sources.locator: Opening TVS convention and Proposition 1 with proof (printed pp1–2); face definition (p12); Theorem 22 complete text and finite-compact-hull subargument (pp13–14, PDF index6). Other intervening results are outside this reading claim.

contents.name: Opening definitions: Hausdorff TVS and local convexity
contents.support: Translate the source convention: Hausdorffness is separate locally.

contents.name: Proposition 1: bounded functional criterion
contents.support: Read full proof; for complex bounds shrink the neighborhood with its inverse image under x↦ix, rather than assume the same neighborhood is rotation invariant.

contents.name: Finite product/simplex subargument in Theorem 22
contents.support: All K_j are compact and convex; local proof spells out grouping and zero weights.

contents.name: Face definition before Theorem 21
contents.support: Face includes convexity; the local x² computation contrasts it with the extremal endpoint property.

contents.name: Theorem 22: Milman converse
contents.reason: The complete displayed argument was read, including the final correction for identical support points. Only its finite-hull supplier belongs in this prerequisite pair; extracted overbars require care in future authoring.
